info.name: Task Management API
info.description:
Full validation flow for the Rust task management API: two-factor login, admin/staff permissions, task assignment, and cache hit/miss behaviour.

## How to use

1. Start the API with `APP_ENV=dev` (folder 2 reads the code from the dev-only mail log route).
2. Set the `baseUrl` variable if you are not on `http://127.0.0.1:3000`.
3. Open the Collection Runner and run the whole collection **in order**. Every token, user id, and task id is captured automatically by the post-response scripts, so nothing needs pasting by hand.

Every request carries assertions, so the Runner doubles as a test report.

Folders 3 onward depend on state created by earlier folders. Start from a fresh database for exact counts: seeding is idempotent, but tasks accumulate across runs.

request.description: Confirms the server is up before anything else runs.

item.name: 1. Setup

request.description: Idempotent: re-running returns the same two ids and changes nothing.

exec: pm.test('admin has the admin role', () => pm.expect(b.admin.role).to.eql('admin'));
pm.test('Bond has the staff role', () => pm.expect(b.staff.role).to.eql('staff'));

item.description: Creates the two fixed accounts. Safe to run repeatedly.

item.name: Step 1 - login (returns a challenge, NOT a token)

request.description: A correct password alone yields nothing usable. This is the point of the flow.

exec: pm.test('does NOT leak the code', () => { pm.expect(b.code).to.be.undefined; pm.expect(b.dev_code).to.be.undefined; });

item.name: Step 2 - read the emailed code (dev only)

request.description: This route exists only when APP_ENV=dev. It stands in for an inbox.

item.name: Step 3a - verify with a WRONG code (expect 401)

request.description: A typo must be rejected without burning the challenge.

item.name: Step 3b - verify with the correct code

request.description: The earlier wrong attempt did not invalidate the challenge.
Replay is distinguishable from an unknown challenge because the row is marked consumed, not deleted.

item.name: Create task 4 - Debrief with Q branch (high)
Create task 5 - File the expense report (low)

request.description: Batch assignment is transactional: an unknown id fails the whole request.
Scoped by email, so it returns Bond's code and not the admin's.

item.name: Step 3 - verify and collect Bond's token
6. Validation - Bond's view and the cache
Bond tries to create a task (expect 403)

request.description: Only admins create tasks. Enforced by the AdminUser extractor before the handler body runs.
THE validation point. Data comes from Postgres; nothing here is hardcoded.

exec: pm.test('cache.hit is false on the first read', () => pm.expect(b.cache.hit).to.eql(false));
pm.test('exactly 3 tasks, not at least 3', () => pm.expect(b.tasks.length).to.eql(3));
pm.test('every task belongs to Bond', () => b.tasks.forEach(t => pm.expect(t.assigned_to).to.eql('jamesbond@example.com')));
pm.test('priorities are high, medium, low', () => pm.expect(b.tasks.map(t => t.priority)).to.eql(['high','medium','low']));

request.description: Comparing only the flag would pass even if the cache served an empty list, so the rows are compared too.

exec: pm.test('cache.hit is true on the second read', () => pm.expect(b.cache.hit).to.eql(true));

item.name: Admin reassigns task 1 away from Bond

request.description: Invalidates the cache for BOTH the previous and the new assignee.
This is what distinguishes a cache wired to the data from one that is merely warm.

exec: pm.test('now exactly 2 - a stale cache would still report 3', () => pm.expect(b.summary.total_assigned_tasks).to.eql(2));

request.description: An update that changes no assignment must still invalidate, because the cached payload embeds task fields.

item.name: view-my-tasks - after the edit (MISS, new title)

exec: pm.test('an edit evicts the cache too', () => pm.expect(b.cache.hit).to.eql(false));
pm.test('the new title is visible, not the cached one', () => pm.expect(b.tasks.map(t => t.title)).to.include('Decode the transmission (urgent)'));

item.name: Bond reads a task he is not assigned (expect 404, not 403)

request.description: 403 would confirm the id exists. The endpoint must not disclose that.

exec: pm.test('does not confirm the id exists', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.not.eql(403));

item.name: Bond renames his own task (expect 403 - status only)
Bond moves the status of his own task (expect 200)

request.description: The one mutation staff are allowed, and only on their own task.
An out-of-range enum is rejected at deserialization and never reaches the database.

item.name: 8. Logout and revocation

request.description: The denylist entry lives in Redis with a TTL equal to the token's remaining lifetime.

exec: pm.test('an unexpired but revoked token must not authenticate', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(401));

item.description: Runs last because it revokes the token the earlier folders rely on.
